writeup: TIC 942471837 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.1452 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 5.14% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal shows high statistical significance with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 209.2, and pixel-level analysis yields a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 17.2. However, a critical uncertainty affects this candidate: the dimming centroid lies only 0.002 pixels closer to the target star than to a nearby bright neighbor, falling within the instrument's stated centroid systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels. This means TESS's resolution cannot confidently distinguish whether the eclipses originate from the target star or its neighbor.
